Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said the country is moving rapidly on the reform express,
and the institutions that conduct examinations must also work on reforms that are the need
of the country.
Addressing the centenary celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission, UPSC,
at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. Mr Modi stressed on the need to bring young people
into public services who are drawn not to public office but to public service. He said today,
21st century India is moving forward with a new work culture and its core principle
is pro-people, pro-active, good governance. Mr Modi said an examination should not be
considered just an event that as it is related to the future of the youth. Mr Modi noted
that a delay of even a few months can create difficulties for the youth and therefore the
examination system should follow the principle of time certainty.

a great extent by institutions such as the UPSC and the State Public Service Commissions.
Mr. Modi said the young people being recruited today will play an important role in building
of Iqquishad Bharat.
The programme marks the culmination of year-long celebrations that commenced on 1 October last
year commemorating 100 years since the establishment of the UPSC in 1926.
Prime Minister Modi has said safeguarding forests and wildlife is essential for maintaining
nature's balance and securing a valuable legacy for future generations.
In his message on the occasion of Wildlife Week 2026, Mr Modi urged citizens to contribute
towards protecting wildlife and their habitats.
From Mr Modi highlighted India's achievements in wildlife conservation over the past decade
citing the success of Project Chita, he also mentioned conservation efforts for species
such as the Great Indian Bustard, Rhinoceros, River Dolphin and Snow Leopard.
Mr Modi highlighted India's role in promoting global cooperation for big cat conservation
through the International Big Cat Alliance.
The government has reduced the stock-holding period for sugar dealers to 15 days and fixed
the stock-holding limit at 1,000 quintals with effect from the 15th of this month.
It will remain effective till November this year.
The Consumer Affairs Ministry said the government has revised the sugar stock-holding
norms to prevent hoarding and ensure smooth supply to consumers during the festive
season.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said the same spirit of synergy and integration currently
being emphasised among the three armed forces needs to be implemented within the financial
framework of the Defence Accounts Department as well, speaking on Defence Accounts Day
in New Delhi today. Mr Singh said if the financial systems are also integrated, the entire defence
management will become even more efficient. The minister urged them to adopt and internalise
the best practices in quality auditing at both the national and international levels
and keep pace with evolving standards across the country and the world.

Only then will this be possible.

An important meeting is being held in New Delhi today under the chairmanship of
Union Home Minister Amit Shah to resolve the long-pending Mahanadi water dispute between
Chhattisgarh and Odisha, more from our correspondent.
The dispute over sharing of Mahanadi waters between Chhattisgarh and Odisha has remained
unresolved for several years.
Odisha had requested the central government in November 2016 to set up a tribunal to
resolve the dispute.
After talks failed to resolve the issue, the Mahanadi water dispute's tribunal
was constituted in March 2018. Odisha says that water projects being built in the upper
reaches of the Mahanadi in Chhattisgarh affect the flow of water to Odisha during the non-Monson
season. Chhattisgarh, on the other hand, has maintained that it needs to use its share
of water for irrigation, industrial and domestic needs. Both states have given a written assurance
to the Central Water Commission that any decision taken by the Commission in the larger
More interest of both states will be acceptable to them.

At the Asian Games, 2026, today, India opened its sailing medal account as Manu,
Francis and Prince Gurusinkal Noble secured silver in the men's kiff competition today,
finishing behind China after nine races.
Indian compound archer Ganesh Manirath Nantiramuru
produced a commanding performance to win the men's individual bronze medal.
Ganesh, who was a part of the gold-winning men's team yesterday,
defeated Vietnam's Khong Duk Thang in the bronze medal playoff
after bowling out of individual gold contention with a semi-final loss.
In squash, India settled for a bronze medal
after losing 1-2 to Hong Kong in the women's team semi-final.
